items.problem: Migrated app degrades DisplayInformation orientation output to 'N/A' + raw exception because DisplayInformation.GetForCurrentView() throws on desktop and the skill offered no working replacement (only a DPI shortcut).
items.evidence: migration-score.json feature 'Show and lock orientation' verdict=partial; discrepancies.md HIGH 'GetForCurrentView must be called on a thread associated with a CoreWindow'; lessons.json failed_apis[0].
items.root_cause: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md #getforcurrentview mapped DisplayInformation only to RasterizationScale/GetDpiForWindow and blanket-claimed 'None of the GetForCurrentView() patterns work', so the agent believed orientation had no desktop equivalent.
items.change: Corrected the #getforcurrentview section: softened the 'None work' preamble to 'the GetForCurrentView() entry point is gone — use a window-scoped factory'; changed the DisplayInformation row to point at Microsoft.Graphics.Display.DisplayInformation.CreateForWindowId(windowId) with DPI shortcut noted as a subset; added a code snippet acquiring windowId and reading CurrentOrientation/NativeOrientation; noted the DispatcherQueue/caching requirement.
items.expected_effect: Agents replace DisplayInformation.GetForCurrentView() with CreateForWindowId(windowId) and report real orientation/DPI instead of a dead fallback.
items.falsifiable_check: On a re-run of any DisplayInformation/orientation scenario, the WinUI app shows real orientation values (not 'N/A'/exception text) and the feature scores pass instead of partial; no GetForCurrentView() residue remains in the migrated code.
